headline: Drupal and CISA list exploited flaws; most federal fix dates are tomorrow, 28 November
plain_summary: Drupal says a second flaw in its core software is being used in attacks, and CISA added ten exploited flaws to its catalogue, with most federal deadlines on 28 November. Confirmed: Swiss officials report their first attacks on critical infrastructure that used AI agents. Researchers say a hacker used an AI agent against Flemish municipalities, though Belgium's cybersecurity centre cannot confirm the figures. Anyone running Drupal, Mitel MiCollab, Xen Orchestra or Juniper Session Smart should act.

items.title: CISA adds ten exploited flaws to KEV: Mitel, Xen Orchestra, Juniper, Danfoss
items.why: Eight of the ten have a federal due date of 28 November and two have 9 December.
items.action: CISA's catalog entries say to apply vendor mitigations as BOD 26-04 requires, or stop using the product if none are available; Mitel advises its fixed MiCollab release and restricting external access to the conferencing component, per Infobae.

items.title: Drupal core flaw CVE-2026-136716 (SA-CORE-2026-019) exploited in the wild
items.why: Drupal rates it highly critical, and sites that left the installer exposed after SA-CORE-2026-017 may already be compromised.
items.action: Drupal advises updating to the fixed version for your release line and running update.php, securing the installer, and checking logs for unauthorized access, especially to the user 1 account.

items.title: Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers on the official SoftwareOK site were tampered with
items.why: The tampered files install a Python-based remote access trojan, and the cause is not yet identified.
items.action: AhnLab advises checking SHA-256 hashes against the official page, reinstalling the latest version, and checking for suspicious Python environments, scheduled tasks and external traffic; reinstalling alone may not remove the RAT.

items.title: PolinRider loader reported in at least 7,609 GitHub repos
items.why: Apiiro estimates the spread, and the loader was force-pushed into open pull requests at three projects; the North Korea link is reported by The Hacker News, not confirmed here.
items.action: StepSecurity advises reviewing October workflow logs and pull-request timelines, requiring approval for workflows from external contributors, keeping VS Code in Restricted Mode for unfamiliar projects, and rotating GitHub, npm, SSH and cloud credentials from a clean machine if the loader ran.

items.title: Swiss cyber office reports first critical-infrastructure attacks using AI agents
items.why: Five cases are confirmed, three affecting critical infrastructure and two of those successful; the source is unclear.
items.action: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (Bacs) advises a clear reduction of internet-reachable systems, the fastest possible security updates, strict access restrictions and full multi-factor authentication.

items.title: Researchers say DeepSeek-driven AI agent took data from Flemish municipalities
items.why: Secutec and SOCRadar report about 1.2 million people affected across 82 municipalities, but the CCB says it cannot confirm the figures.
items.action: Secutec and SOCRadar say multi-factor authentication and IP restrictions held off the attacks; SOCRadar published detection rules and indicators for IT teams to search their logs.

items.title: Binance says October 29 theft began with a fake job interview
items.why: Binance says an engineer was given a coding assignment containing malware; the FBI attribution to TraderTraitor is reported by BleepingComputer.
